exams.name: Texas Optometry/Therapeutic Optometry Licensing Examination
exams.notes: Board may use a national testing organization for the written portion; examination must include pharmacology and related pathology.
exams.jurisdiction: state board (may use national testing organization for written portion)
exams.quote: A person must pass the examination given by the board to be licensed to practice therapeutic optometry in this state.

interval_years.quote: A license under this chapter is valid for a term of one or two years as determined by board rule.

required.quote: An optometrist or therapeutic optometrist must complete 16 hours of study each calendar year, of which at least six hours must be in the diagnosis or treatment of ocular disease.

hours_per_period.quote: An optometrist or therapeutic optometrist must complete 16 hours of study each calendar year

period_years.quote: An optometrist or therapeutic optometrist must complete 16 hours of study each calendar year

value: at least 6 hours in the diagnosis or treatment of ocular disease
topical_requirements.quote: at least six hours must be in the diagnosis or treatment of ocular disease

available.quote: The board may issue a license to practice therapeutic optometry without requiring the applicant to pass all or part of the examination required by Section 351.253 if: (1) the applicant is licensed in good standing as a therapeutic optometrist in another state

requirements.value: Applicant must be licensed in good standing as a therapeutic optometrist in another state, have passed an equivalent or superior examination, have been actively engaged in practice or full-time teaching for at least five of the seven preceding years, have no pending disciplinary actions, and have never had license suspended or revoked.
requirements.quote: the applicant is licensed in good standing as a therapeutic optometrist in another state; the applicant has passed an examination that is equivalent or superior to the examination required by Section 351.253

credential_type.quote: A person may not practice optometry or therapeutic optometry unless the person holds a license issued under this chapter.

is_mandatory.quote: A person may not practice optometry or therapeutic optometry unless the person holds a license issued under this chapter.

title_protection.quote: Unless a person is licensed to practice under this chapter, the person may not: (1) offer to practice optometry or therapeutic optometry; (2) represent to others that the person is authorized to practice optometry or therapeutic optometry; or (3) use in connection with the person's name a designation implying that the person practices optometry or therapeutic optometry.

scope_protection.quote: A person may not practice optometry or therapeutic optometry unless the person holds a license issued under this chapter.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Fraud, deceit, dishonesty, or misrepresentation in the practice of or seeking admission to optometry/therapeutic optometry
disciplinary_grounds.quote: the applicant or license holder is guilty of fraud, deceit, dishonesty, or misrepresentation in the practice of optometry or therapeutic optometry or in seeking admission to that practice

disciplinary_grounds.description: Unfitness or incompetence by reason of negligence
disciplinary_grounds.quote: the applicant or license holder is unfit or incompetent by reason of negligence

disciplinary_grounds.description: Conviction of a misdemeanor involving moral turpitude or a felony
disciplinary_grounds.quote: the applicant or license holder has been convicted of a misdemeanor involving moral turpitude or a felony

disciplinary_grounds.description: Development of an incapacity preventing practice with reasonable skill and safety
disciplinary_grounds.quote: the applicant or license holder has developed an incapacity that prevents or could prevent the applicant or license holder from practicing optometry or therapeutic optometry with reasonable skill, competence, and safety to the public

disciplinary_grounds.description: Directly or indirectly employing or procuring an unlicensed person to practice optometry
disciplinary_grounds.quote: the license holder has directly or indirectly employed, hired, procured, or induced a person to practice optometry or therapeutic optometry in this state without a license

disciplinary_grounds.description: Aiding or abetting an unlicensed person in the practice of optometry
disciplinary_grounds.quote: the license holder has directly or indirectly aided or abetted an unlicensed person in the practice of optometry or therapeutic optometry

disciplinary_grounds.description: Placing license at the disposal or service of an unlicensed person
disciplinary_grounds.quote: the license holder has placed the holder's license at the disposal or service of, including lending, leasing, or renting to, a person not licensed to practice optometry or therapeutic optometry in this state

disciplinary_grounds.description: Willful or repeated violation of the chapter or board rules
disciplinary_grounds.quote: the applicant or license holder has wilfully or repeatedly violated this chapter or a board rule adopted under this chapter

disciplinary_grounds.description: Willfully or repeatedly representing authorization to cure or treat eye disease beyond statutory authorization
disciplinary_grounds.quote: the license holder has wilfully or repeatedly represented to a member of the public that the license holder is authorized or competent to cure or treat an eye disease beyond the authorization granted by this chapter

disciplinary_grounds.description: Right to practice suspended or revoked by a federal agency for cause warranting board action
disciplinary_grounds.quote: the license holder has had the right to practice optometry or therapeutic optometry suspended or revoked by a federal agency for a cause that the board believes warrants that action

disciplinary_grounds.description: Acting to deceive, defraud, or harm the public
disciplinary_grounds.quote: the applicant or license holder has acted to deceive, defraud, or harm the public
the applicant or license holder is guilty of gross incompetence in the practice of optometry or therapeutic optometry

disciplinary_grounds.description: Pattern of practice demonstrating willful provision of substandard care
disciplinary_grounds.quote: the applicant or license holder has engaged in a pattern of practice or other behavior demonstrating a wilful provision of substandard care

disciplinary_grounds.description: Sexual abuse, misconduct, or exploitation with a patient or unethical abuse of the doctor-patient relationship
disciplinary_grounds.quote: the applicant or license holder has committed an act of sexual abuse, misconduct, or exploitation with a patient or has otherwise unethically or immorally abused the doctor-patient relationship

disciplinary_grounds.description: Prescribing, selling, or distributing controlled substances for other than accepted diagnostic or therapeutic purposes
disciplinary_grounds.quote: the applicant or license holder has prescribed, sold, administered, distributed, or given a drug legally classified as a controlled substance or as an addictive or dangerous drug for other than an accepted diagnostic or therapeutic purpose

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failure to report relocation of office within 30 days
disciplinary_grounds.quote: the applicant or license holder has failed to report to the board the relocation of the applicant's or license holder's office not later than the 30th day after the date of relocation, whether in or out of this state

disciplinary_grounds.description: Practicing or attempting to practice while license is suspended
disciplinary_grounds.quote: the license holder has practiced or attempted to practice optometry while the license holder's license was suspended

definition_quote.value: Practice of therapeutic optometry means using objective or subjective means, not including surgery or laser surgery, to determine or measure the powers of vision of the human eye, examine or diagnose visual defects, abnormal conditions, or diseases of the human eye or adnexa, prescribe or fit lenses or prisms, administer or prescribe a drug or physical treatment, or treat the visual system.
definition_quote.quote: "Practice of therapeutic optometry" means using objective or subjective means, not including surgery or laser surgery, to: (A) determine or measure the powers of vision of the human eye as provided by Section 351.355; (B) examine or diagnose visual defects, abnormal conditions, or diseases of the human eye or adnexa; (C) prescribe or fit lenses or prisms to correct or remedy a defect or abnormal condition of vision as provided by Section 351.356; (D) administer or prescribe a drug or physical treatment in the manner authorized by this chapter; or (E) treat the visual system, including the eye or adnexa as authorized by this chapter.

value: determining or measuring powers of vision
diagnosing visual defects and diseases of the eye and adnexa
prescribing or fitting lenses or prisms
administering or prescribing drugs or physical treatment (therapeutic optometrists only)
treating the visual system including eye and adnexa (therapeutic optometrists only)
methods_authorized.quote: An optometrist or therapeutic optometrist may: (1) perform: (A) vision therapy; (B) hand-eye coordination exercises; (C) visual training; and (D) developmental vision therapy

drug_authority.value: Therapeutic optometrists may administer or prescribe ophthalmic devices, procedures, and appropriate medications by topical or oral means; may prescribe not more than one three-day supply of Schedule III, IV, or V controlled substances; may inject medication for anaphylaxis; optometric glaucoma specialists may additionally prescribe oral/parenteral medications for glaucoma. Basic optometrists may not prescribe drugs.
drug_authority.quote: A therapeutic optometrist may: (1) administer, perform, or prescribe ophthalmic devices, procedures, and appropriate medications administered by topical or oral means, in accordance with this section and Section 351.3581, to diagnose or treat visual defects, abnormal conditions, or diseases of the human vision system, including the eye and adnexa

surgery_prohibited.quote: A therapeutic optometrist may not perform surgery or laser surgery.

surgery_definition.value: A procedure using instruments, including lasers, scalpels, or needles, in which human tissue is cut, burned, vaporized, or otherwise altered by any mechanical means, laser, or ionizing radiation. Includes procedures requiring closing by suturing, clamping, or another device. Does not include a noninvasive procedure to remove a superficial foreign body in the conjunctiva, eyelid, or corneal epithelium that has not perforated the Bowman's membrane.
surgery_definition.quote: "Surgery" means a procedure using instruments, including lasers, scalpels, or needles, in which human tissue is cut, burned, vaporized, or otherwise altered by any mechanical means, laser, or ionizing radiation. The term includes procedures using instruments that require closing by suturing, clamping, or another device. The term does not include a noninvasive procedure to remove a superficial foreign body in the conjunctiva, eyelid, or corneal epithelium that has not perforated the Bowman's membrane.

foreign_body_removal_authorized.quote: The term does not include a noninvasive procedure to remove a superficial foreign body in the conjunctiva, eyelid, or corneal epithelium that has not perforated the Bowman's membrane.

glaucoma_treatment_authorized.quote: A therapeutic optometrist may not administer or prescribe an oral or parenteral medication or treat glaucoma unless the therapeutic optometrist holds a certificate issued by the board.

anaphylaxis_treatment_authorized.quote: A therapeutic optometrist may inject appropriate medication for a patient who has an anaphylactic reaction to counteract the anaphylaxis. The therapeutic optometrist shall immediately refer the patient to a physician.

vision_therapy_authorized.quote: An optometrist or therapeutic optometrist may: (1) perform: (A) vision therapy; (B) hand-eye coordination exercises; (C) visual training; and (D) developmental vision therapy

value: May prescribe not more than one three-day supply of Schedule III, IV, or V controlled substances
Schedule I and II controlled substances are not authorized
controlled_substance_schedule_restrictio.quote: A therapeutic optometrist may prescribe not more than one three-day supply of any medication classified as a controlled substance under Schedule III, IV, or V of 21 U.S.C. Section 812.

opioid_prescription_day_limit.quote: A therapeutic optometrist may prescribe not more than one three-day supply of any medication classified as a controlled substance under Schedule III, IV, or V of 21 U.S.C. Section 812.

oral_pharmaceutical_authority.quote: administer, perform, or prescribe ophthalmic devices, procedures, and appropriate medications administered by topical or oral means

pharmaceutical_certification_required.quote: A therapeutic optometrist may not administer or prescribe an oral or parenteral medication or treat glaucoma unless the therapeutic optometrist holds a certificate issued by the board.

tiered_license_types.quote: "Optometrist" means a person licensed under this chapter and authorized to practice optometry. ... "Therapeutic optometrist" means a person licensed under this chapter and authorized to practice therapeutic optometry.

specialty_certification_types.quote: A therapeutic optometrist certified under this section shall be known as an optometric glaucoma specialist.

pharmacology_training_hours_required.quote: The board by rule shall require successful completion of accredited academic and clinical courses in pharmacology and related pathology that are ... determined by the board to be equivalent in the total number of classroom hours to the requirements for other health care professionals in this state who are licensed to use pharmaceutical agents, including dentists, podiatrists, and physicians.

supervised_clinical_internship_required.quote: To obtain a certificate, a therapeutic optometrist must: (1) complete an instructional clinical review course; and (2) pass an examination approved by the board.

referral_to_physician_required.quote: A therapeutic optometrist shall refer a patient to an ophthalmologist if: (1) the patient is younger than 16 years of age and has been diagnosed as having glaucoma

home_visit_permit_required.quote: A person may not practice optometry or therapeutic optometry from house to house or on the streets or highways ... Subsection (a) does not prohibit an optometrist, therapeutic optometrist, or licensed physician from attending, prescribing for, or providing eyeglasses or ophthalmic lenses to a person: (1) who, because of illness or physical or mental infirmity, is confined to the place the person resides; or (2) in response to an unsolicited request or call for those services.

spectacle_prescription_release_required.quote: If, after examining a patient, an optometrist or therapeutic optometrist believes that lenses are required to correct or remedy a defect or abnormal condition of vision, the optometrist or therapeutic optometrist shall: (1) inform the patient; and (2) provide the patient with a copy of the patient's spectacle prescription.

limited_teaching_license_available.quote: The board by rule may issue a limited license to a full-time clinical faculty member of an institution of higher education of this state who provides instruction in optometry or therapeutic optometry.

retired_license_status_available.quote: The board by rule may allow a license holder to place the person's license on retired status.

criminal_background_check_required.quote: The board shall require that an applicant for a license submit a complete and legible set of fingerprints, on a form prescribed by the board, to the board or to the Department of Public Safety for the purpose of obtaining criminal history record information from the Department of Public Safety and the Federal Bureau of Investigation.
